title: Blade Runner 2049 Spinner
subtitle: A Spinner study staged in a rain-soaked future city atmosphere.
summary: Blade Runner Spinner 2049 is a cinematic vehicle and environment study inspired by the scale, haze, and neon industrial mood of Blade Runner 2049.
description: The project centers on a Spinner concept set against dense city forms, brutalist massing, atmospheric lighting, and high-contrast urban silhouettes.
The image set combines vehicle renders, city compositions, character-focused studies, and process-oriented frames from the project archive.

title: Displacement Experiments
subtitle: Procedural surface studies exploring displacement, material stress, and abstract terrain.
summary: Displacement Experiments is a 2017 series of procedural 3D studies built around surface deformation, texture-driven geometry, and abstract material behavior.
description: The series explores displacement as both a modeling technique and a visual language. Height maps, procedural textures, and material response push simple forms into ridges, fractures, ripples, and terrain-like surfaces.

Rather than treating the tests as isolated renders, the image set reads like a small archive of material behavior: glossy folds, eroded geometry, stressed surfaces, and abstract structures caught between sculpture, landscape, and simulation.

The work sits at the intersection of technical experiment and cinematic image-making, using procedural surface detail to create tactile forms that feel photographed, manufactured, and unstable at the same time.

title: Resonance Field
summary: Resonance Field is an audio-reactive motion study created in TouchDesigner, translating the Blade Runner 2049 theme into a living field of procedural movement, light, and signal-like texture.
description: The piece uses audio input as the driver for motion, intensity, and visual modulation, turning rhythm and frequency into a reactive system rather than a fixed animation.

Built in TouchDesigner, the video explores the relationship between sound, generative structure, and cinematic abstraction. Pulses, distortions, and evolving forms respond to the track as if the image is being performed in real time.

title: The Sinner in Me
summary: The Sinner in Me is an audio-reactive TouchDesigner visual built to Depeche Mode's song of the same name, turning the track's dark pulse into a live field of signal paths, distortion, and unstable light.
description: The video uses Depeche Mode's "The Sinner in Me" as the driving source, letting rhythm, pressure, and atmosphere shape a dark map of connected traces.

Built in TouchDesigner, the piece treats sound as a control system. Lines gather, drift, and fracture around a central threshold, moving between surveillance diagram, ritual mark, and reactive waveform.
The latest pass leans into a colder signal aesthetic: faint cartographic labels, chromatic edge noise, and a tightening field of white paths that feel pulled toward the word "free" at the center.

title: Imaginary Circles
summary: One rotating point, all the way to quantum mechanics. Imaginary Circles is a set of interactive interface studies that visualizes circular geometry, radians, waves, and logarithmic spirals as cinematic educational systems.
description: The project turns foundational circle concepts into dark, high-contrast interface compositions built for exploration. Each study isolates a different mathematical behavior and presents it through motion, annotation, and luminous diagram language.

The collection includes a circle-to-wave transform, a radian measurement study, and a logarithmic spiral study, all connected by a shared visual system of measured arcs, precise typography, and atmospheric depth.
The result sits between field guide, motion reference, and interactive learning tool: a compact system for making abstract geometry feel spatial, tactile, and cinematic.

title: Cinematic Field Guide
summary: Cinematic Field Guide is a working reference for lighting and camera decisions, collecting photometric units, exposure, color temperature, and cross-engine light-intensity values for Octane, Redshift, and Unreal Engine 5.
description: The project is built as a practical cheat sheet for moving between real-world cinematography language and digital lighting systems. It gathers the values that tend to get scattered across notes, docs, and renderer-specific habits: lumens, lux, nits, exposure behavior, color temperature, and equivalent light settings across engines.

Instead of treating the information as a plain table, Cinematic Field Guide presents it as a dense reference interface. Lighting categories, camera values, real-world fixture examples, and renderer translations are organized into a dark technical surface designed for quick comparison while building a shot.

The goal is to make lighting decisions feel less arbitrary across Octane, Redshift, and Unreal Engine 5. The guide gives artists a shared baseline for matching physical lights, evaluating exposure, and translating a cinematographer’s language into usable digital settings.

title: Overcast
summary: Overcast is a Grand Isle tactical conditions report for fishing, combining live weather, marine conditions, tides, solunar timing, and species-coded fishing grounds into one cinematic field interface.
description: The project pulls together the kinds of information anglers usually have to check across several places: NWS current conditions and forecast, NOAA tides and water levels, wind and visibility, solunar activity windows, and mapped fishing zones around Grand Isle.

Instead of treating that data as a standard weather page, Overcast presents it like an operational screen. Forecast cards, marine readouts, tide context, moon timing, and fishing-ground markers are organized into a dense interface that can be scanned quickly while still feeling atmospheric and tactile.

The Mapbox layer gives the piece its field-report character, plotting fishing grounds and species-coded spots against a coastal map. The teal, low-light visual language keeps the system tied to overcast marine conditions: technical, damp, local, and built around the practical question of whether the water, weather, and timing are worth the trip.
format: Live fishing and marine conditions dashboard

images.alt: Overcast cinematic weather dashboard with forecast cards and atmospheric interface overlays

title: The Four of Us Are Dying
summary: The Four of Us Are Dying is an audio-driven motion piece built to Nine Inch Nails, using Cinema 4D sound modifiers, X-Particles, and After Effects to translate the track into procedural movement and atmosphere.
description: The piece uses Nine Inch Nails' "The Four of Us Are Dying" as the audio source, allowing the track's tension, rhythm, and tonal shifts to drive the visual system.

Built with sound modifiers in Cinema 4D, X-Particles, and After Effects, the project treats audio as a force acting on form. Particle behavior, motion intensity, and composited atmosphere respond to the music, creating a reactive visual study that sits between procedural animation and music video language.

title: Black Noise
summary: Black Noise is an audio-reactive TouchDesigner piece built to Nine Inch Nails song of the same name, translating the track into procedural motion, distortion, and dense signal texture.
description: The video uses Nine Inch Nails' "Black Noise" as the audio source, turning the track's abrasive energy and rhythmic pressure into a reactive visual system.

Created in TouchDesigner, the piece treats sound as a live input for motion, intensity, and image disruption. Forms pulse, smear, and fracture in response to the music, creating a dark generative study that sits between abstract signal processing and music visualization.

title: When I'm Small
summary: When I'm Small is an audio-driven motion piece built to Phantogram, using Cinema 4D, X-Particles, and After Effects to turn the track into procedural movement, particle behavior, and layered atmosphere.
description: The video uses Phantogram's "When I'm Small" as the audio source, translating the song's pulse and mood into a reactive visual structure.

Created with Cinema 4D, X-Particles, and After Effects, the piece uses sound-influenced motion and particle systems to build a dense audiovisual study. The result sits between music visualization, procedural animation, and cinematic motion design.

title: Long After Dark
summary: Long After Dark is a collaborative title sequence concept created with [Liz Margiotta](https://www.lizmargiotta.design/) for a fictional vampire series set in New Orleans.
description: The piece imagines the opening titles for a southern gothic vampire story, using New Orleans as the emotional and visual foundation: nocturnal streets, ritual atmosphere, old architecture, heat, shadow, and the feeling that something is moving just outside the frame.

Built as a mood-driven title sequence study, the project focuses on pacing, typography, texture, and cinematic restraint. The collaboration shaped the concept into a dark, atmospheric identity for a series that feels intimate, haunted, and rooted in place.

title: Data Haven
subtitle: A black-box city of encrypted storage towers and magenta signal logic
summary: Data Haven is a cinematic cube-city study built from stacked black data blocks, glowing magenta interface marks, shallow focus, and dense label systems.
description: The series treats storage, identity, and machine-readable signage as architectural mass. Tall black modules become a miniature data district, with printed interface fragments, QR-like markings, and luminous pink indicators suggesting a private network of sealed information.
The selected frames emphasize macro scale, depth of field, reflective surfaces, and the contrast between soft photographic blur and precise technical labeling.

title: White Noise Telemetry
summary: White Noise Telemetry is a monochrome HUD/FUI study built from luminous scan lines, blurred diagnostic panels, and layered instrument readouts suspended in depth.
description: The series pushes interface graphics toward a photographic, overexposed signal aesthetic. Dense panels, buffer labels, calibration readouts, and graph structures are treated like glass, light, and optical noise instead of flat UI elements.
The restrained black-and-white palette emphasizes depth of field, bloom, and parallax, creating a technical display system that feels observed through a lens rather than rendered directly on screen.

title: Signal Lattice
summary: Signal Lattice is a cinematic HUD/FUI study built around dense orange navigation overlays, scan readouts, and layered glass-panel interface depth.
description: A compact interface study focused on parallax, opacity, grid density, and warm avionics-style system graphics. The sequence explores how abstract readouts and targeting structures can feel tactile and dimensional when treated like photographed glass rather than flat UI.

title: Ravens Isle
summary: Ravens Isle is a short cinematic built in Unreal Engine 5, set on a storm-battered island fortress clinging to sea cliffs. Towers rise through the fog, lightning fractures the horizon, and ravens circle against a cold teal sky.
description: The only signs of life are the dim flicker of candlelit windows and the wind snapping at the battlements and slow figure moving between the boats. The piece is a study in atmosphere, pushing Lumen global illumination and Ultra Dynamic Sky's storm system to build a scene that feels genuinely foreboding. No dialogue, no characters. Just the island, the storm, and the silence beneath it.
Color graded in DaVinci Resolve through a Linear-ACES pipeline with Dehancer film emulation, pulling the image toward cold, overexposed highlights and deep crushed shadows.

title: Desert Silence
summary: Desert Silence is a short cinematic piece exploring solitude and atmosphere in a sun-bleached desert environment. Built entirely in Unreal Engine 5 using Lumen global illumination and volumetric lighting, the film follows the quiet of an ancient desert settlement and crumbling architecture, wind-swept dunes, and the stillness of a figure alone by fire as night falls.
description: Color graded in DaVinci Resolve through a Linear-ACES pipeline with Dehancer film emulation, bringing a textured, analog warmth to the renders. No post-compositing, what you see came out of the engine.

title: Dark Star
summary: Dark Star is a short cinematic built in Unreal Engine 5, set in the gravitational pull of a collapsing star. Capital ships drift in the foreground as light bends around a dying sun, its accretion disk casting copper and amber across the debris field. A moon tumbles slowly through the middle distance. Nothing explodes. Nothing attacks. Just the weight of something enormous, slowly ending.
description: The piece explores scale and stillness in deep space, using Space Creator Pro and Lumen to build a physically grounded environment where the lighting does all the storytelling. Color graded in DaVinci Resolve through a Linear-ACES pipeline.

title: Temple of the Sun
summary: Temple of the Sun is a short cinematic built in Unreal Engine 5, set deep within a forgotten Hindu temple complex reclaimed by forest and time. Light breaks through the jungle canopy in thick shafts, falling across ancient columns, cracked stone, and still water. The staircase rises toward something just out of reach. The film moves between two states of the same space — the temple as it once stood, and the ruin it became. No characters, no conflict. Just light, atmosphere, and the weight of something sacred slowly returning to the earth. Rendered with Lumen global illumination and Nanite geometry, color graded in DaVinci Resolve through a Linear-ACES pipeline with Dehancer film emulation.
description: Temple of the Sun uses architecture as the main storytelling device, balancing hard-edged forms with dust, warmth, and ritual atmosphere.
The project studies how light can define the emotional read of a place before the viewer understands its function.

title: Haunted Swamp
summary: Haunted Swamp is a short cinematic built in Unreal Engine 5, set in the dead of a fog-choked night somewhere deep in the American South. A plantation house sits back from the tree line, its windows burning with dim candlelight. Bare branches cut across the frame. Gravestones disappear into the mist. Nothing moves. Nothing has to.
description: The piece leans entirely on atmosphere — volumetric fog, Lumen-lit interior light spilling through glass, and Ultra Dynamic Sky's overcast night system doing the heavy lifting. The color treatment keeps everything cold and desaturated except for those amber windows, which draw the eye like the only warmth left in the world.
Color graded in DaVinci Resolve through a Linear-ACES pipeline with Dehancer film emulation.

title: Cold Warnings
summary: Cold Warnings is a short cinematic built in Unreal Engine 5, set at a remote arctic research station at the edge of the world. Massive radio dishes tilt toward a sky that offers nothing back. A cargo plane sits forgotten in the snow. Somewhere in the base, lights are still on. Nobody answers.
description: The piece is built entirely around unease, the kind that comes not from what you see but what the environment implies. A station this equipped, this isolated, still running but completely still. Ultra Dynamic Sky handles the overcast arctic conditions, with Lumen pulling every surface into a cold, flat light that leaves nowhere to hide.
Color graded in DaVinci Resolve through a Linear-ACES pipeline with Dehancer film emulation.

title: Ghost Signals
summary: A short cinematic built in Unreal Engine 5, inside a city still broadcasting to no one.
description: Neon cuts through haze that has no origin. Signage scrolls across a figure who doesn't look up. Somewhere above the alley, a screen cycles through an advertisement for something that no longer exists. The infrastructure of communication, running perfectly, with nothing left to say. The city isn't abandoned. It just stopped requiring an audience.

The look comes from deliberately broken optics. Anamorphic 50mm glass that halates and streaks in neon light, chromatic aberration at the frame edges, gate weave, light leaks that arrive uninvited. Lumen pulls the color across wet surfaces and into the dark between buildings.

The KitBash3D Cyberpunk kit and Bigmediumsmall's Tokyo Alley Artis series build the world, everything rendered in-engine, no compositing after the fact. The imperfections aren't added. They're what the glass remembers.
Color graded in DaVinci Resolve.

title: The Colony
summary: A perpetual lunar sunset, built in Unreal Engine 5, set at Shackleton Extraction Facility on the lunar south pole; a He-3 and hydrogen mining operation on the Gerlache Ridge.
description: Not everyone made it back inside.

Lighting is entirely practical, the sun locked two degrees above the horizon, raking across the regolith and never moving. No atmosphere to scatter it, no air to carry sound. Lumen handles the bounce into the shadowed undercuts, the only warmth in the frame.
Environment built with Kitbash3D Minerva and Space Colony kits. Astronauts by BigMediumSmall Astronova.
Color graded in DaVinci Resolve through a Linear-ACES pipeline with Dehancer film emulation.

title: Deep Orbit Studies
subtitle: Wide-screen spacecraft and planetary environment studies
summary: Deep Orbit Studies is a cinematic space concept series built around spacecraft silhouettes, planetary scale, orbital light, and quiet deep-space atmosphere.
description: The sequence moves between spacecraft passes, distant planets, ring systems, and horizon-scale compositions, treating space as a place of mass, silence, and controlled graphic shape.

The work focuses on wide-screen framing, restrained color, and the relationship between engineered forms and celestial bodies, with each frame reading like a production still from a larger speculative world.

title: Knight and Squire
summary: This storyboard sequence explores the classic Batman and Robin dynamic within a rain-soaked Gotham, emphasizing pursuit, teamwork, and iconic silhouettes. The action centers on a high-speed vehicle chase featuring the Batmobile and Batcycle, using cinematic framing and clear spatial storytelling to contrast Batman’s power with Robin’s agility. The sequence focuses on mood, scale, and action clarity while staying true to the visual language and mythology of Batman and Robin, communicating tone, pacing, and visual intent in a concise, production-ready format.

title: Hangar 5
subtitle: A 3D environment built in Cinema 4D, inside a facility that services things too large to fully see.
summary: The number on the wall tells you there are at least four others. A ground crew figure stands near the landing strut of something that fills most of the frame, not inspecting it exactly, just present near it, the way people stand near things they can't do much about. Pipes run everywhere, purposefully or not. The amber light suggests heat, or age, or both. Whatever comes and goes from here, it isn't small.
description: The piece was rendered using Arnold's toon shader in Cinema 4D, which reduces light and shadow to crisp, graphic silhouettes rather than reaching for photorealism. The environment is built from Bigmediumsmall's Modelshop Greebles, hundreds of modular sci-fi hull components, panels, and mechanical clusters assembled into a space that reads as operational rather than decorative. The toon pass makes the density of the kit legible in a way photorealism often buries.

title: Aerospace HUD
subtitle: A layered targeting system, built frame by frame
summary: Somewhere between the clouds and whatever comes next, a system wakes. Concentric rings materialize from nothing. Data resolves at the edges. A reticle finds its center. The target is already there before the acquisition is confirmed.
description: Aerospace HUD is a motion design exercise in information architecture and threat geometry. Each frame was constructed as a discrete state: dormant, boot, loading, active, alert, critical. The design language draws from real avionics aesthetics — dashed bounding brackets, hexagonal sensor housings, cascading status lines, a targeting bloom that moves from neutral to thermal red as lock progresses. No transitions were assumed. Every layer was built to hold independently before compositing into sequence.

The HUD overlay was designed entirely in Adobe Illustrator, animated and staged in After Effects, with final compositing in Photoshop. No AI generation. No stock overlays. Every element drawn from scratch.

title: HUD Schema Signal
subtitle: Generated interface schematics staged as cinematic signal space
summary: A dense HUD and FUI study built from generated SVG and PNG interface systems, then staged in Cinema 4D and rendered through Octane as layered signal glass, reticles, readouts, and acquisition geometry.
description: HUD Schema Signal treats the interface as a physical field instead of a flat overlay. Vector schematics, generated PNG elements, reticle systems, grid states, and small typographic data fragments are arranged in depth so the camera moves through information rather than simply looking at it.

The project was assembled from generated SVGs and PNGs, staged in Cinema 4D, and rendered with Octane. The result sits between heads-up display design, fictional user interface language, and abstract information architecture.

title: Redline Acquisition
subtitle: A redline targeting field built from layered HUD geometry
summary: A cinematic HUD and FUI render study built around red acquisition arcs, nested reticle systems, dense telemetry fields, and glass-like interface depth.
description: Redline Acquisition extends the HUD schema series into a warmer, more urgent signal state. White reticle rings and calibration ticks sit inside red sweep geometry, while background telemetry, brackets, scale marks, and alphanumeric fragments recede into a layered targeting field.

The selected frames emphasize the strongest range of the set: a full system overview, oblique camera passes, macro reticle details, and atmospheric depth-of-field studies. The artwork was staged in Cinema 4D and rendered with Octane from generated SVG and PNG interface elements.

title: Data Cubes
subtitle: Procedural forms that hold light
summary: Isolated forms rendered in pure void. Emissive edges catch teal and amber light against absolute black, implying a system without explaining what it does. No ground plane. No sky. Nothing to give it context and nothing that needs any.
description: Data Cubes is a procedural object study built in Cinema 4D and rendered in Octane. Inspired by the work of Toros Kose, the piece explores how much a single geometric form can hold before it stops being abstract.
Color graded in DaVinci Resolve through an ACES pipeline.

title: Futuristic Interface Substrate
subtitle: EMMISIVE STRUCTURES
summary: Isolated forms rendered in pure void. Emissive edges catch teal and amber light against absolute black, implying a system without explaining what it does. No ground plane. No sky. Nothing to give it context and nothing that needs any.
description: Inspired by the procedural work of Toros Kose, this series explores how much a single geometric form can hold before it stops being abstract. The substrate suggests circuitry, architecture, topography — never committing to any of them. Each frame is a study in emissive restraint: how little light it takes to make something feel inhabited.
Color graded in DaVinci Resolve through an ACES pipeline.

title: F-35 Scan
subtitle: The geometry of acquisition.
summary: The system doesn't search. It confirms. A silhouette resolves out of noise, brackets find their edges, and the geometry of acquisition assembles itself one layer at a time.
description: F-35 Scan is a study in information design of how a strategic operation might analyze a threat through a visualization.
Designed and rendered entirely in Cinema 4D with Octane. No AI generation. No stock elements. Every layer constructed from scratch.

title: Grid State
subtitle: Maximum signal. Zero known source.
summary: There are architectures that exist below the interface — lattices of logic and light that process without pause, indifferent to the presence of anyone watching. Grid State is a descent into that space. Glass panels catch signals that have no origin. Dot matrices hold patterns that suggest meaning without offering it. The red is not a warning. It was always red.
description: Every surface was built and lit without shortcuts. No AI generation, no stock compositing — geometry, glass materials, and volumetric light authored from scratch to feel like something that exists somewhere, running something, for reasons that remain unspecified.
Color graded through DaVinci Resolve on an ACES pipeline with Dehancer film emulation over an S-Log3 base.

title: Libération!
summary: Paris, August 1944, The Liberation of Paris during World War II. For this one I really wanted that found footage feeling like something that was actually shot on Super 8 by someone who happened to be there.
description: The base world is a game environment that I pushed further with Kitbash3D elements, and the Tiger I is from TurboSquid, weathered and placed close enough to the lens that the grain does the rest.

I added hardware Ray Tracing with Lumen doing the heavy lifting on atmosphere along with Ultra Dynamic Sky adding the “fog of war.” Color graded in DaVinci Resolve, sitting in faded amber and ash with the fire allowed to blow out the way old film always did.
No AI, no compositing all particles are in engine.

title: Outbreak
summary: An abandoned hospital after an outbreak from a mysterious disease and nothing seems to be left behind. Color graded in DaVinci Resolve through a Linear-ACES pipeline with Dehancer film emulation.

title: Medieval Village
summary: A cinematic medieval village environment shaped through atmospheric lighting, period detail, and immersive visual storytelling.

title: The Wastelands
summary: A cinematic journey through a desolate wasteland, built around ruined environments, atmospheric light, and post-apocalyptic visual storytelling.

title: MSY // Sector Asset
summary: A real-time aviation data interface centered on Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport, bringing live aircraft tracks, weather, movement logs, carrier activity, and system telemetry into a cinematic command display.
description: The interface transforms live Airplanes.live aircraft data, Open-Meteo weather, and Carto/OpenStreetMap mapping into a focused operational view of New Orleans airspace.
Monochrome typography, grid overlays, event logs, and aircraft detail panels create a functional FUI system that balances dense information with legibility and atmosphere.

title: Elemental Blocks
summary: An interactive periodic table that turns all 118 elements into an explorable system of atomic data, practical applications, nucleosynthesis stories, and synthesized sound.
description: Each tile presents atomic number, mass, electron configuration, oxidation states, category, and phase, then opens a detailed view with common applications, discovery history, and name origin.
The sonification system maps atomic number to pitch, period to octave, and chemical category to chord shape and waveform, giving every element a distinct synthesized voice.

title: Outbreaks: Global Epidemic Intelligence
summary: A multi-page epidemic intelligence and data-visualization system combining current surveillance, outbreak geography, pathogen history, pandemic research, and two millennia of disease records.
description: The live dashboard organizes active outbreak signals, geographic hotspots, risk, chronology, and case trajectories into an editorial surveillance atlas designed for dense but legible reading.

Linked Chronicle and Great Plagues features extend the system into historical storytelling, while the Epidemic Record compares 29 pathogens across 2,000 years through an interactive radial visualization with scaled, equal, and individual disease views.

title: Neurodegenerative: Alzheimer MRI Review
summary: An interactive clinical-orientation interface for reviewing Alzheimer-associated structural MRI patterns, cognitive regions, and research indicators within a dense, cinematic diagnostic display.
description: The system combines an axial MRI contact sheet with selectable hippocampal, ventricular, cortical, and amyloid review layers, structural disease markers, regional correlation, and a continuously updating analysis log.

ADNI, OASIS, and HCP references provide the research context. All measurements and scores are demonstration values for interface exploration, and the experience is presented as a visual orientation model rather than diagnostic output.

title: Cargo Meridian // Middle East
summary: An interactive freight-network interface mapping active shipments, shipping routes, and logistics assets across the Middle East in a cinematic operational display.
description: The regional map connects Gulf ports and inland hubs with bilingual geographic labels, live shipment positions, route status, and operational metrics for load, fuel, and estimated arrival.
Shipments, Routes, and Assets views reorganize the same network into focused logistics panels, balancing dense transportation data with a restrained amber command-interface aesthetic.

title: TRANSIT // LIVE
summary: An interactive near-Earth-object tracking system visualizing orbital paths, upcoming close approaches, and potentially hazardous objects across the inner solar system.
description: TRANSIT organizes NASA and JPL near-Earth-object data into a live heliocentric display, combining an interactive Three.js orbital model with approach distance, velocity, estimated diameter, magnitude, and encounter timing.

Selecting an object connects its trajectory to a dedicated procedural model and risk profile, while the approach log and timeline keep safe and potentially hazardous encounters legible within a dense cinematic command interface.

title: LEXICON — Vocabulary Observatory
summary: An interactive vocabulary-estimation instrument that combines adaptive word testing, immediate linguistic context, and editorial typography in a focused learning interface.
description: LEXICON samples core through rare vocabulary across selectable quiz lengths, updating a provisional word estimate as users identify definitions and move through increasing levels of difficulty.

Each answer reveals pronunciation, etymology, useful neighboring terms, and an antonym, while recently studied words become a quiet reading list. Serif display typography and structured sans-serif controls give the educational experience an editorial, observatory-like character.

title: MissionLaunch — Upcoming Space Missions
summary: A live mission-operations interface connecting upcoming launch windows, orbital spacecraft, provider activity, and countdown data in one global command display.
description: MissionLaunch organizes a live launch feed into mission-type and agency filters, pairing upcoming vehicles, providers, pads, launch status, and countdowns with a mapped view of orbital infrastructure.

Tracked spacecraft including the ISS, Hubble, JWST, Sentinel, and TDRS reveal dedicated orbital context, while the launch timeline and agency-load display make dense mission scheduling legible at a glance.

title: Capitol Ledger — Political Finance Observatory
summary: A political-finance observatory separating public disclosure records, calculated market estimates, asset relationships, and benchmark comparisons in a dense analytical interface.
description: Capitol Ledger maps a curated demonstration dataset of political financial disclosures into ranked records, ownership lanes, sector allocation, issuer context, and disclosure-to-market-value flows.

Sorting and owner filters expose gains, losses, disclosed size, recency, and performance relative to the S&P 500. Method notes, confidence ratings, source plans, and separate valuation lanes keep official records distinct from calculated estimates and indirect exposure; the project does not allege misconduct.

title: Every Moment Votes — 2026 Midterm Elections
summary: A non-partisan civic information experience connecting the 2026 U.S. midterm election to national races, Louisiana turnout, close historical margins, and practical voting resources.
description: Every Moment Votes turns sourced election data into an editorial journey from the national ballot to the voter’s immediate community. Maps compare House representation and 2026 Senate contests before focusing on Louisiana’s 64 parishes and midterm participation.

A state-by-state Senate guide, historic close-election margins, turnout comparisons, and official registration links make the stakes tangible without endorsing candidates or parties. National figures cite public research and election sources; parish-level dot sizes and turnout shading are illustrative design data.

title: Landfall — Tropical Cyclone Operations
summary: A Gulf of Mexico tropical-cyclone operations interface combining forecast tracks, coastal conditions, historical hurricanes, and regional exposure in a cinematic command display.
description: Landfall organizes tropical weather intelligence into a dense operational dashboard centered on the Gulf Coast. The primary map combines projected paths with basin status, New Orleans weather, Gulf water temperatures, tide gauges, advisories, and storm-signal references.

Interactive historical tracks reveal peak wind, minimum pressure, landfalls, and recorded fixes for major hurricanes, while a Gulf-city risk index compares coastal exposure. The experience draws on NHC, NWS, NOAA CO-OPS, map, radar, and satellite sources to connect live monitoring with historical context.

title: SPEC//FORGE — Procedural Asset Generator
summary: A seed-driven design instrument for generating production-ready cyberpunk graphics, interface panels, labels, posters, and contact sheets from a flexible visual system.
description: SPEC//FORGE turns modular layouts, palettes, symbols, recurring language, and controlled randomness into a fast generative workflow. Users can lock or reroll a seed, select from interface and editorial archetypes, tune format and grain, and create individual assets or dense contact sheets.

A curated symbol library and reusable vocabulary keep each result visually related while preserving variation. Finished compositions export as editable SVG files or pixel-accurate 2× PNGs, connecting exploratory interface design with practical production output.
